content.text: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod. My name is Marco. My name is Catherine and today we have a lesson for you all about life at home and life with your parents.
content.trans: 你好，大家，欢迎来到英语课堂。我的名字叫马科，我叫凯特琳，今天我们要学习关于在家生活和与父母相处的技巧。

content.text: That's right. We've all lived with our parents when we were younger or maybe we still do. And of course they have certain rules in the house and well when you break those rules something happens. There are consequences and that's what's happening in today's dialogue.
content.trans: 是的，我们都有在父母身边生活过。当我们年轻的时候，他们可能也有自己的规矩。当然，他们家里也有一些规则，比如你违反了这些规矩，会发生什么。然后就会有后果，这就是今天对话中的情况。

content.text: So let's take a listen to this dialogue and when we come back we'll be talking more about what's going on and what some of these words and phrases mean.
content.trans: 所以，让我们听听这段对话吧，我们下次回来时会多聊一聊发生了什么以及这些词语和短语的含义。

content.text: Do you know what time it is?
content.trans: 你知道现在是什么时间吗？

content.text: Um, ten.
content.trans: 嗯，十。

content.text: Get in this door young man. It's midnight. You are two hours past curfew.
content.trans: 进来看看小伙子。现在是午夜了，你已经超出了宵禁两个小时了。

content.text: I know, but it wasn't my fault. I told Jennifer she had to drop me off before ten, but she wouldn't leave the party.
content.trans: 我知道，但不是我的错。我告诉珍妮弗她必须在十点之前把车给我开，但她就是不肯离开聚会。

content.text: I don't care. You are grounded for life, mister.
content.trans: 我不管。你这辈子都得待在那，先生。

content.text: Mom, that is so unfair.
content.trans: 妈妈，那真是太不公平了。

content.text: You know the rules and you broke them. No allowance and no TV for a week. I usually never ground you, but this time I have to put my foot down.
content.trans: 英语：你了解这些规则，然后你破坏了它们。没有允许权和无电视的限制。我通常不会让你下课，但这次我必须给你一个教训。

content.text: What? For being a couple of hours late, you have to be kidding.
content.trans: 你这是为什么，才差两个小时就迟到呢？这都开玩笑了吗？

content.text: I don't want to hear it. Now go to your room.
content.trans: 我就不想听了。现在去你的房间吧。

content.text: All right, we're back. So a very typical case somebody or the kid returns home. It's too late and now they're in trouble.
content.trans: 好的，我们回来了。所以，一个典型的例子，有人或孩子回家了。太晚了，现在他们遇到了麻烦。

content.text: Yes, his parents are not very happy in this case. It's his mom who is telling him what the consequences will be.
content.trans: 是的，他的父母对此并不高兴。是妈妈在告诉他后果会是什么样子。

content.text: So let's take a look at language takeaway and find out what some of these keywords are.
content.trans: 当然，让我们一起来看看语言小贴士，看看这些关键词是什么。

content.text: Language takeaway.
content.trans:
语言小贴士。
中文：这是一份语言学习的提示。

content.text: All right, so the first word that we're going to take a look is actually something that his mom said and he said that you are two hours past curfew.
content.trans: 好的，我们接下来要看看的第一个词确实是他说的那句话。他妈妈说你已经超出了禁晚归时间两个小时了。

content.text: Curfew. So curfew has to do specifically with the time when your parents expect you at home.
content.trans: 宵禁。所以宵禁是指你的父母希望你什么时候回到家的时间点。

content.text: That's right. So if your curfew is ten o'clock, you have to be home before or by ten o'clock.
content.trans: 没错。所以如果你的宵禁是十点，你必须在十点之前或者正好十点回家。

content.text: Right. So in this case, if the boy's curfew is ten o'clock and he arrives home at midnight, 12 o'clock, he's two hours past curfew.
content.trans: 好的。在这种情况下，如果男孩的宵禁时间是晚上十点，他十一点到家的话，他已经超出了宵禁时间两个小时了。

content.text: That's right. And even sometimes cities or governments will implement certain curfews at certain times.
content.trans: 没错。有时候甚至城市或政府会在特定时间实施某些宵禁。

content.text: That's right. And I don't think adults really have curfews at home.
content.trans: 没错。我觉得成年人在家里根本不会有宵禁的规定。

content.text: No, I don't think so. It depends on what you want. But kids definitely have curfews.
content.trans: 不，我觉得不一定。这要看你想什么。但孩子肯定有宵禁时间。

content.text: What happens though, Marco, when you break curfew?
content.trans: 哎，Marco，你打破了宵禁怎么办？

content.text: So this is a very serious offense and you're going to get punished. And the way that we say this, usually parents to their children, you are grounded or you ground that kid.
content.trans: 这个是非常严重的错误，你将会受到惩罚。我们通常说，父母把孩子“禁足”或者“禁足”那个孩子。

content.text: Okay, so you might have heard this word one talking about airplanes or flights at an airport. The plane was grounded.
content.trans: 好的，你可能听说过这个词，它和机场里的飞机有关。那架飞机被停飞了。

content.text: It basically means it can't go anywhere. And so when you're talking about a kid or a person, you basically mean, okay, you're grounded.
content.trans: 基本上就是不能去任何地方。所以当你说到孩子或者人的时候，你基本上是说，好吧，你就被禁足了。

content.text: You can't go out with your friends. You can't go anywhere. Usually you can go to school.
content.trans: 你不能和朋友出去。你也别想去哪。通常你可以去学校。

content.text: Right, right. But you can't have fun is the meaning.
content.trans: 好的，没错。但是你不能玩乐的意思是。

content.text: That's right. So it's usually a fixed phrase. You're grounded. That means that you are punished. You can't go out.
content.trans: 没错。所以通常是一个固定短语。你被禁足了。这意味着你要受到惩罚，不能出门。

content.text: But in this case, the mom specifies saying you're grounded. So that means that he can't go out.
content.trans: 但这种情况，妈妈说你被禁足了。所以这意味着他不能出门。

content.text: But on top of that, she said no allowance and no TV for a week.
content.trans: 但是，她还说一周内不给零花钱和不开电视。

content.text: So the mom and so allowance is the money that your parents give you to go out like to go to the movies or something.
content.trans: 所以，妈妈和零花钱就是你们父母给你用来出去的那笔钱，比如去电影院或者做其他事情。

content.text: And your parents might give this to you on a weekly basis. So every Saturday you get $5 or on a monthly basis every month you get $20.
content.trans: 你的父母可能会每周给你送这个。所以周六你就能得到五块钱。每个月，你每月都能拿到二十块钱。

content.text: And when his mother says you're not going to have any allowance for a week, that means we're not going to give you any money this week.
content.trans: 当他妈妈说你这一周不要任何零用钱的时候，这意味着我们这一周不会给你发工资。

content.text: Right. So that is in allowance. How much money you get per month or per week.
content.trans: 好的。所以那是在允许范围内的。你每个月或者每周能领多少钱？

content.text: The key thing about allowance though is that it's not something you do for work. You don't work and receive allowance.
content.trans: 其实，假期补助金并不是你为了工作而做的。它不是你工作后才得到的报酬。

content.text: If you work, you have a salary allowance is something that you get for free from someone.
content.trans: 如果你工作，你就会得到一笔工资津贴，这是别人给你免费的。

content.text: Yeah. So you can get an allowance from your boss to eat. But you can also have an allowance from your parents to do fun things.
content.trans: 是的。你爸给你报销吃饭的钱，而你妈可以帮你拿钱做些好玩的事情。

content.text: That's right. So usually kids obviously they can't work. So they get an allowance from their parents usually for fun things like going to the movies and stuff.
content.trans: 没错。所以通常孩子们显然不能工作。他们从父母那里得到一笔零花钱，用来买电影票和其他好玩的事情。

content.text: Exactly. Alright now going back a little bit, let's take a look at two ways that the mom addressed or called her son because obviously it's her son.
content.trans: 没错。现在回过头来，我们来看看妈妈是如何称呼或者叫她的儿子的。显然，那是她自己的儿子。

content.text: But when he got home she said get in this door young man.
content.trans: 但是当他回到家时，她说你这个年轻人，进这扇门。

content.text: Okay, these are angry mom phrases. When you're in trouble your parents tend to use different words to talk to you.
content.trans: 好的，这些都是愤怒的妈妈用的话。当你遇到麻烦时，你的父母通常会使用不同的词汇和方式来与你交流。

content.text: So this is a very popular one young man. Right. So it's like saying you should be mature but you made a mistake.
content.trans: 所以这可是个很受欢迎的小伙子。对了，说你应该是成熟稳重一点，结果你就犯了一个错误。

content.text: Alright so come inside right now young man. Yeah, it's a it's a way to kind of emphasize that you are also very angry.
content.trans: 好的，你现在就进来吧，小伙子。对了，这有点儿意思，因为你可以表达出你也很生气的样子。

content.text: And also when he was trying to explain what happened she said I don't care. You're grounded for life, Mr.
content.trans: 而且，当他试图解释发生的事情时，她只是说我不在乎。你这辈子都不得翻身了，先生。

content.text: You're grounded for life, Mr. So these are both ways of talking to young boys. Mr. is the opposite of Miss.
content.trans: 你这辈子都被禁足了，老兄。这两个都是跟小男孩说话的方式。Mr. 是Miss的反义词。

content.text: But in the case of a young girl you'd say get in this door young lady. Right. And then you're grounded for life, Missy.
content.trans: 但是，对于一个年轻的小姑娘来说，你可以说“进来吧，小姑娘。”对。然后你就永远没法动了，Missy。

content.text: Missy? Yeah, I think they say Missy. Missy. So Missy Mr. Young Man young lady. These are always referring to people in kind of it's weird.
content.trans: 英语：Missy？对，他们说的正是Missy。Missy先生、小姐、女士。这些总是指人的一种方式是有点奇怪的。

content.text: It's kind of like their adults but they're not. Yeah, that's right. That's like saying you're in trouble. Yeah. So a very interesting thing going on here with this young man who got grounded.
content.trans: 英语：它有点像他们的成年人，但他们不是。没错，这就是说你处于困境。对，这里发生了一件有趣的事情，这个年轻人被扣上了什么。

content.text: All right, we're back. So now let's take a look at four key phrases that we've picked out for you on fluency builder.

content.text: Fluency builder. All right. So this first phrase is something that actually we hear when the young boy or the young man is giving his excuse for being late.

content.text: He said, Listen, I told Jennifer she had to drop me off before ten. That's right. So the phrasal verb there is to drop off.
content.trans: 他说，听着，我告诉詹妮弗她必须在十点之前把我送到那里。没错的。那个短语的意思是drop off。

content.text: This means to leave someone somewhere. That's right. But usually it means to drive someone to a certain place. So for example, Jennifer probably has a car.
content.trans: 这个就是让人去某地的意思。对了，通常是指开车把某人送到某个地方。比如说，吉娜肯定有一辆车。

content.text: And Jennifer was supposed to take this boy home. So he said she was going to drop me off before ten o'clock. That means kind of leave him at his house.

content.text: That's right. So the verb is to drop off. But we usually insert the subject in between. So to drop me off. She is going to drop me off.

content.text: I dropped him off at the bank. That's right. All right. So now that Jennifer was supposed to drop him off at ten. That didn't happen. So he got grounded.

content.text: He's upset and she's angry and she said, Listen, I have to put my foot down. What does this mean? You put your foot on the ground. It's strange to hear this phrase.

content.text: It means that she's going to be strict. That she's not going to let him just get away with it or not ground him. She really has to be strict and she has to punish him.
content.trans: 这句话的中文翻译是：

content.text: Okay. So to put your foot down or I put my foot down, this means to be strict with someone to not maybe bend the rules or be flexible.
content.trans: 好的。所以要硬气一点，或者我来硬气，这就意味着对某人要求严格，不一定要遵守规则或灵活变通。

content.text: So for example, my mother was always very, very loose with my brother. He could do what he wanted or whatever. But one day he did something really horrible and she finally put her foot down.
content.trans: 所以，例如，我的母亲总是非常松散地与我弟弟相处。他可以做什么就做什么或者什么也不做。有一天，他做了件非常糟糕的事情，并最终把脚放下了。

content.text: And she grounded him. She grounded him for three months.
content.trans: 她把他停了三个月。

content.text: All right. So that's what happens when somebody puts their foot down. And now obviously he was very surprised that he's going to be grounded for so long.
content.trans: 好的。那么，就是这样一种情况发生了。现在很明显，他因为这种行为非常惊讶，因为他被处以这么长时间的禁足。

content.text: And only for being a couple of hours late. So he said, you have to be kidding. You have got to be kidding. So this is a rhetorical. So he's not talking about joking here.
content.trans: 而且是短暂的两小时迟到。他说道，你必须开玩笑。你必须开玩笑。这是讽刺。所以这里不是玩笑。

content.text: He's saying, no way. I can't believe it. This is not happening to me. Yeah, you're not serious. You're not serious. So he's upset. And I would be too. No one likes to be grounded.
content.trans: 英语：他正在说，不可能。我无法相信这是真的。这不发生在我的身上。对，你不是在开玩笑。你不是在开玩笑。所以他说的很伤心。而且我也很伤心。没有人喜欢被绑住。

content.text: But he's saying, okay, come on. No way. That's too serious. That's right. So this is what this is a phrase that you can use with someone if you're not really believing what they're saying or you're surprised. You have to be kidding me.
content.trans: 但是他说，好的，来吧。不行。那太严肃了。对的。所以这就是你如果不能相信他们的话，或者你很惊讶的时候，可以使用这个短语。如果你不认为他们说的是真的，或者你很惊讶，那么我必须说，哈哈。

content.text: Yeah, but usually there's also a degree of anger. So you're upset at the decision. For example, I'm watching the the world cup right now. And there was a foul. And I was very upset because I didn't think it was a foul. And I said, you have got to be kidding me.
content.trans: 是的，但通常还有点生气。所以你气愤的是这个决定。比如我现在正在观看世界杯。然后有一粒黄赌球。我非常气愤，因为我没想到这是个黄赌球。我说，你得给我打退堂鼓。

content.text: That's right. Okay. So that's exactly the way that we would use that phrase. And well, obviously the mother had made up her mind. She's very decided. And she said, I don't want to hear it.
content.trans: 是的。明白了。所以这就是我们用来这个短语的方式。而且很明显，母亲已经做出了决定。她非常坚定。她说：“我不想要听这句话。”

content.text: So this is the end of the conversation. Okay. This is one of those phrases that will just stop anything you're talking about. So they're arguing and she says, nope, I don't want to hear it. That means no more excuses. No more talking. This is the end.

But if you have authority like your apparent or your boss, you can say, nope, I don't want to hear it. I have made my decision.

content.trans: 我倾向于认为女孩更容易受到惩罚。我不太确定是因为她们好，还是因为她们更擅长隐藏他们父母的意图。

content.text: Yeah, maybe. Because whenever I would come home, my mother would always wake up, but she doesn't really understand what time it is.
content.trans: 是的，可能。因为我每次回家的时候，妈妈总是会醒过来，但她其实不太懂时间是什么意思。

content.text: So I'd say, oh, Mom, it's 11 o'clock. Good night. It'd be like four o'clock in the morning and she had no idea.
content.trans: 英语：所以我说，哦，妈妈，现在是11点了。早上好！她不知道。

content.text: So who was the person or the parent that put their foot down? Was it your mom or your dad?
content.trans: 是哪位大人或妈妈/爸爸硬撑住了呢？是你妈妈还是你爸爸？

content.text: It's my dad. What's the serious one? Oh, really? Yeah, it's interesting because sometimes it's the dad that's very strict and the mom kind of helps you out and tries to kind of not get you grounded or something.
content.trans: 英语：它是我的爸爸。那这个严肃的呢？哦，真的吗？是啊，挺有意思的，因为有时候爸爸很严格，妈妈会帮你出一些主意，或者尽量不让你受到约束。

content.text: But sometimes it's the other way around. The mom is really strict and firm and the dad's like, come on, don't ground him.
content.trans: 但有时候情况正好相反。妈妈真的很严格，爸爸就只是说：“来吧，别关他。”

content.text: They're just having fun. Well, I think in some families, the children understand who is strict and who is maybe not so strict.
content.trans: 他们只是玩得开心。嗯，我觉得在一些家庭里，孩子们大概能理解谁比较严格，谁可能不太那么严格。

content.text: And so they say, oh, well, Mom said that it's okay. So I think maybe you should let me go out and the dad will be very angry because the mother said that it's okay.
content.trans: 所以他们说，嗯，妈妈说没事。所以我觉得你可能应该让我出去，爸爸会很生气，因为妈妈说没事。

content.text: That's right. All right. So that's all the time we have for today. We're really curious to get your stories. Maybe tell us why were you grounded or how long were you grounded for?
content.trans: 正确。好的。今天我们的时间已经用完了。我们真的很想知道你的故事。或许你可以告诉我为什么被地雷绑住了，或者你被绑住的多长时间了？

content.text: Or what was your curfew when you were a child or growing up? Our website is engluchpa.com. We hope to see you there.
content.trans: 你小时候或长大后，你的宵禁是什么时候？我们的网站是engluchpa.com。我们希望在那里见到你。

content.text: All right. We'll see you guys there. Bye.
content.trans: 好的。我们到时候见。拜拜。

content.text: Thank you.
content.trans: 好的。
